chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mis'mam said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and I said: 'I am praying and a young girl passes by me, and perhaps I embrace her.' He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm (permissible/does not invalidate)

ai.seo_question: Does embracing a young girl invalidate my prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith illustrates the practical flexibility (rukhas) in Shia jurisprudence regarding minor physical interactions during prayer. It establishes that casual embrace of a young girl does not break the state of prayer, reflecting a nuanced view of distraction versus nullification. This ruling is often cited to demonstrate the balance between ritual purity and everyday social realities in Shia legal theory.
